topic_angle: お風呂で転ばないために見直したいこと3つ
topic_angle_en: Three things to review so you do not slip and fall in the bath

target_viewer.living_situation: lives alone or with minimal daily support
target_viewer.daily_context: bathes daily in a standard Japanese unit bath (ユニットバス or traditional 浴室), may already have minor balance or mobility concerns but is still independent
target_viewer.information_need: wants a calm, plain-language checklist of specific things to inspect and adjust in the bathroom to reduce fall risk without major renovation

viewer_problem: 多くのシニアの方は、毎日のお風呂が少し不安になっても、具体的にどこを確認すればいいのか分からないまま入浴を続けています。大きなリフォームではなく、すぐにできる見直しポイントを知りたいと感じています。
viewer_problem_en: Many seniors continue bathing with growing unease but do not know exactly which spots to check. They want actionable review points they can handle without major renovation.
working_promise: お風呂まわりで見直しておきたいポイントを3つに絞って、ひとつずつ一緒に確認していきます。大掛かりな工事ではなく、今日からできる小さな見直しが中心です。
working_promise_en: We will walk through three specific review points around the bath, one by one. The focus is on small adjustments you can start today — not major renovation.

this_video_claims: 浴室には転倒リスクを高めるポイントがいくつかある
足元・手すり・温度差の3つは、自分で見直せる代表的なチェック項目
小さな見直しでも安心感につながることがある
不安が大きい場合は、家族や専門家に相談するとよい
this_video_does_NOT_claim: これで転倒を完全に防げる
手すりをつければ絶対安全
ヒートショックはこの方法で防げる
医師の指導なしでも十分
リフォーム不要で全て解決

forbidden_claims: 「絶対に転ばない」—absolute fall prevention promise
「ヒートショックを防げます」—heat shock prevention certainty
「医者は教えてくれない浴室の秘密」—anti-doctor conspiracy framing
「薬いらずのお風呂術」—medication replacement framing

research_questions.question: 日本の高齢者における浴室内転倒の主な原因と発生状況（消費者庁・厚生労働省・東京消防庁等の統計）
research_questions.question_en: Leading causes and incidence of bathroom falls among Japanese seniors — statistics from Consumer Affairs Agency, MHLW, Tokyo Fire Department

research_questions.question: 浴室の床材・滑り止めマットの転倒予防効果に関するエビデンスまたは推奨（住宅改修ガイドライン等）
research_questions.question_en: Evidence or recommendations on anti-slip flooring and bath mats for fall prevention — housing modification guidelines

research_questions.question: 浴室手すりの設置位置・種類に関する介護保険制度の推奨と自治体支援制度
research_questions.question_en: Recommended grab bar placement and types under the long-term care insurance system and municipal support programs
research_questions.source_type_expected: MHLW care insurance guideline, municipal government page

research_questions.question: ヒートショックのメカニズムと予防のための浴室・脱衣所の温度管理の推奨（日本救急医学会等）
research_questions.question_en: Heat shock mechanism and recommended bathroom/changing room temperature management — Japan Association for Acute Medicine etc.
research_questions.source_type_expected: medical society guideline, NHK health article

research_questions.question: 高齢者が自分でできる浴室安全チェックリスト（自治体や介護予防事業の配布資料）
research_questions.question_en: Self-check bathroom safety checklists distributed by municipalities or fall prevention programs
research_questions.source_type_expected: municipal pamphlet, care prevention program material

research_questions.question: 浴室リフォーム・住宅改修の介護保険適用範囲と自己負担の概要
research_questions.question_en: Scope of long-term care insurance coverage for bathroom renovation and out-of-pocket cost overview
research_questions.source_type_expected: government official page, care manager resource

notes_for_research: RQ1 — prioritize Consumer Affairs Agency (消費者庁) accident statistics and Tokyo Fire Dept (東京消防庁) rescue data for bathroom falls
RQ2 — check if JIS standards exist for bathroom anti-slip flooring in residential settings
RQ3 — confirm current care insurance (介護保険) coverage rate for grab bar installation (typically 1割 self-pay)
RQ4 — use Japan Circulation Society or Japan Association for Acute Medicine guidelines on safe bathing temperature; cite 41°C recommendation
RQ5 — look for municipal PDF checklists (e.g., Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Osaka City) as visual reference for script structure
RQ6 — do NOT frame renovation as mandatory; present as an option with professional consultation emphasis
General — all statistics should be from the last 5 years when possible; older data acceptable if it is the most recent official source
